3: Instructions for AI agents (Claude Code and similar) working in this repository.
4: 
5: ## What this project is
6: 
7: **Dungeon Haul** is a remake of a TOJam 8 local multiplayer sidescroller: four haulers loot a dungeon, navigate traps, sabotage each other, and split the haul via **Share Modifiers**. This remake makes **online multiplayer first-class** (authoritative server, drop-in/reconnect, AI fill for empty seats).

38: ## Product freezes (do not re-open without ADR + owner OK)
39: 
40: From [`docs/decisions/ARCHITECT-OPEN-QUESTIONS.md`](docs/decisions/ARCHITECT-OPEN-QUESTIONS.md):
41: 
42: | Topic | Decision |
43: |---|---|
44: | Platforms | Desktop evergreen browsers only (Chrome / Firefox / Safari / Edge) |
45: | Matchmaking | Private room codes only for MVP |
46: | Couch co-op | Online seats first; local multi-gamepad is stretch |
47: | Level progression | Random unplayed pair at each fork (not full path graph for MVP) |
48: | Resolution | **960×540** logical, integer scale, letterbox |
49: | Hosting | Fly.io (or Railway) sticky processes for game rooms |
50: | Identity | No accounts; ephemeral names + high-score initials |
51: | Run length | `levelsAfterHoard` configurable; default **2** for playtests, **7** full |
52: | Characters | Soft-unique (prefer distinct; allow clash) |
53: | Pause | No global pause in MVP (local menu only) |
54: 
55: Also fixed by architecture:
56: 
57: - Exactly **4** hauler seats in game state; AI fills inactive/disconnected seats
58: - Client never computes official takes — only displays server `ScoreReport`
59: - Share formula: `take = totalTreasure × (shares_i / sum shares)` with **min 1 share**
60: - Rules package is pure (no Phaser, Colyseus, Node `fs`)
61: 
62: ## Stack (binding)
63: 
64: See [`docs/decisions/ADR-001-tech-stack.md`](docs/decisions/ADR-001-tech-stack.md) and ADR-002.
65: 
66: | Layer | Choice |
67: |---|---|
68: | Client | Phaser 3 + TypeScript + Vite |
69: | Server | Node.js/TypeScript + **Colyseus** rooms (authoritative sim, 30 Hz) |
70: | Shared | `packages/rules` (pure), `packages/protocol` (messages) |
71: | Lobby / REST | Hono (or Fastify) |
72: | Persistence | PostgreSQL (high scores) |
73: | Monorepo | pnpm workspaces (or npm workspaces) |
74: | Deploy | Docker; Fly.io-class sticky WebSocket rooms |
75: 
76: **Rejected for game loop:** peer-to-peer host, pure serverless rooms without sticky WS, FastAPI as sim authority (dual-language rules drift).

108: ## How agents should work
109: 
110: ### Orientation
111: 
112: 1. Read this file and [`docs/README.md`](docs/README.md).
113: 2. For gameplay rules, prefer design PDF + `rules-engine` design + `share-modifier-api` over inventing numbers.
114: 3. For netcode behavior, prefer ADR-002 + `netcode-messages.md` + `simulation` design.
115: 
116: ### Implementation
117: 
118: - Work in **small, task-sized PRs** aligned to `TASKS.md` IDs (e.g. `C07-T03`).
119: - Prefer **parallel work behind frozen interfaces**; mock peers when blocked.
120: - Keep `packages/rules` pure and heavily unit-tested (seeded RNG, golden fixtures).
121: - Server owns truth: collisions, inventory, trap hits, fork tallies, end scores.
122: - Client predicts movement only; never invent inventory or takes.
123: - Use fixed-timestep simulation; cap large frame deltas (no quantum tunneling).
124: - Determinism: seed treasure/fork RNG; record input tapes for headless sim tests.
125: 
126: ### Testing
127: 
128: Follow [`docs/testing/AUTOMATED-TEST-STRATEGY.md`](docs/testing/AUTOMATED-TEST-STRATEGY.md):
129: 
130: - **Vitest** for unit/contract/headless sim (not dual Jest unless ADR changes it)
131: - **Playwright** for later E2E
132: - Component cases live in each `TEST-PLAN.md`; integration scenarios in `INTEGRATION-TEST-PLAN.md`
133: - Flaky unit tests: fix or quarantine — do not silent-retry unit suites
134: - Target high coverage on `packages/rules`; presentation may be lighter
135: 
136: ### Art / audio
137: 
138: - Asset Inventory & Spec: [`docs/art/ASSET-INVENTORY.md`](docs/art/ASSET-INVENTORY.md)
139: - Asset Production & Completion Status: [`docs/art/ASSET-STATUS.md`](docs/art/ASSET-STATUS.md)
140: - Asset Pipeline & Phaser 3 Developer Guide: [`docs/art/PIPELINE-AND-PHASER-GUIDE.md`](docs/art/PIPELINE-AND-PHASER-GUIDE.md)
141: - Production Web Assets: Served at `client/public/assets/` (`manifest.json`, WebP texture atlases, background images)
142: - Master High-Res Originals: Retained in `art_raw/` (uncompressed masters for editing/changes)
143: - Aesthetic: side-view 2D, cartoon haulers, biome themes; **no isometric**
144: - **Python Pipeline Scripts (`scripts/`)**:
145:   - `asset_processor.py` — Core utility module (chroma key background removal, frame scaling, Phaser 3 JSON Hash atlas generator).
146:   - `slice_treasures.py` — Slices P0 primary treasures into `atlas_treasures`.
147:   - `generate_and_process_treasures_sets.py` — Generates & processes secondary loot sets (Celestial, Divine, Song, Veg, Box) into `atlas_treasures_sets`.
148:   - `slice_tiles.py` — Slices MVP tiles, switches, gates, and traps into `atlas_tiles_mvp`.
149:   - `process_lava_biome.py` — Generates & packs Lava biome assets into `atlas_tiles_lava`.
150:   - `generate_ice_biome.py` — Generates & packs Ice biome assets into `atlas_tiles_ice`.
151:   - `process_cavern_tiles.py` — Generates & packs Cavern biome assets into `atlas_tiles_cavern`.
152:   - `generate_mist_pack.py` — Generates & packs Mist biome assets into `atlas_tiles_mist`.
153:   - `generate_and_process_enemies_traps.py` — Generates & packs Golem, Phantom, Lightning, Gas, Rock into `atlas_enemies`.
154:   - `generate_ui_icons_pack.py` — Generates & packs D-pad/buttons, medals, badges, and spinner loop into `atlas_ui_icons`.
155:   - `generate_and_process_vfx.py` — Generates & packs particle VFX sheets (stun stars, spill, flashes, dust, poof) into `atlas_vfx`.
156:   - `slice_characters.py` — Slices 4 character animation sheets (Gnome, Sprite, Halfling, Dwarf) into `char_*` atlases.
157:   - `generate_char_extras.py` — Generates & packs Title stick walk-ins, Argue/Rummage poses into `atlas_char_extras`.
158:   - `generate_and_process_level_props.py` — Generates & packs background props (torches, banners, candelabras, grates) into `atlas_level_props`.
159:   - `process_screens.py` — Resizes and converts screen background artwork to 960×540 WebP images.
160: 
161: ### Documentation hygiene
162: 
163: - Keep `docs/` the source of truth for design; update docs when behavior intentionally changes
164: - Prefer ADRs for stack/hosting/netcode decisions
165: - Do not rewrite the source PDFs
166: - Do not put secrets in docs or code; use env/secrets for DB URLs
167: 
168: ## Suggested monorepo layout (when code lands)
169: 
170: ```text
171: /
172: ├── CLAUDE.md
173: ├── docs/                 # design package (exists)
174: ├── packages/
175: │   ├── rules/            # pure TS — share modifiers, treasure value
176: │   └── protocol/         # message types, shared enums
177: ├── client/               # Phaser + Vite
178: ├── server/               # Colyseus room + lobby REST + sim
179: ├── content/levels/       # pixel maps + meta
180: └── ...
181: ```
182: 
183: If the tree differs, update this section and ARCHITECTURE.md together.
184: 
185: ## Game flow (quick)
186: 
187: ```text
188: Title / Credits / High Scores (idle attract)
189:   → Lobby (create/join code, claim character, ready)
190:   → Instructions (human drop-in practice; no AI)
191:   → Level 0 Hoard
192:   → Fork (argue / path vote) ↔ Level … until levelsAfterHoard done
193:   → End (count haul → share titles → spoils → optional name entry)
194:   → High Scores
195: ```
196: 
197: Controls (NES-like): run, jump, duck/pickup, trip/push, drop/throw treasure. Full tables in design PDF and input interface docs.
198: 
199: ## Out of scope unless asked
200: 
201: - Mobile / touch MVP
202: - Required user accounts / OAuth
203: - Public matchmaking queues
204: - Peer-to-peer or host-migration multiplayer
205: - Flash / Flixel runtime
206: - Global pause for online sessions
207: - Expanding to full 19-level path graph before MVP ships
208: 
209: ## When stuck
210: 
211: 1. Check frozen decisions and the component DESIGN.
212: 2. Check interface contracts — do not invent a parallel protocol.
213: 3. Ask the user for product clarifications (architecturally ambiguous fun/balance choices).
214: 4. For pure rule conflicts: **design doc §2.3 share tables win** over premise section duplicates (see rules-engine DESIGN).
215: 
216: ## Success criteria for agents
217: 
218: A good contribution:
219: 
220: - Matches a named task or test case ID
221: - Respects authority boundaries (server truth / pure rules / dumb presentation)
222: - Adds or updates tests where logic is pure or sim-critical
223: - Leaves docs consistent if contracts change
224: - Does not expand MVP scope past freezes

1: # Dungeon Haul — Aesthetic Brief
2: 
3: > **Status:** Documentation only (no binary art).  
4: > **Sources:** TOJam 8 design document (§1–§5 mockups), [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md) (960×540 logical, Phaser, placeholder atlas), [COMPONENTS.md](../COMPONENTS.md) (C-02 presentation).  
5: > **Scope:** Side-view 2D only. No isometric. No 3D.
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## 1. Elevator pitch (visual)
10: 
11: Four cartoon haulers (Gnome, Sprite, Halfling, Dwarf) race a loot-stuffed sidescroller dungeon. Read like a playful NES-era heist: **control clarity first**, gold lust second, slapstick third. Think stick-figure energy with enough silhouette and color coding that four players never lose their character at a glance.
12: 
13: ---
14: 
15: ## 2. Visual pillars
16: 
17: | # | Pillar | Implication for art |
18: |---|---|---|
19: | **V1** | **NES control clarity** | Huge readable hitboxes of intent: haulers, treasure tops, spikes, switches. Prefer chunky outlines over fine hatching. UI glyphs match NES pad mental model (D-pad, A, B). |
20: | **V2** | **Playful dungeon heist** | Cartoonish, not grimdark. Traps threaten comedy (spill treasure Sonic-style), not gore. Gold gleams; characters bounce. |
21: | **V3** | **Stick → hauler silhouette** | Title mockup: simple haulers carrying letter blocks. Full game characters keep that readable body language (big head/body contrast, clear carry stack above head). |
22: | **V4** | **Biome as mood, not noise** | Each biome has a short palette and 3–5 signature decor props. Gameplay midground stays legible; parallax carries flavor. |
23: | **V5** | **Four-player color coding** | Each hauler owns a primary hue used on body, HUD, share panels, high-score portraits. Never rely on hue alone for critical traps (also use shape). |
24: | **V6** | **Letterboxed fixed canvas** | All composition designed for **960×540** logical pixels, integer scale (1×/2×/3×). No UI elements that break outside safe margins. |
25: 
26: ---
27: 
28: ## 3. Style constraints
29: 
30: ### 3.1 Line, form, shading
31: 
32: | Rule | Spec |
33: |---|---|
34: | Projection | Strict **side-view orthographic** 2D. No 3/4 view, no isometric floor tiles. |
35: | Outline | 1–2 px dark outline on characters/treasure/traps at 1× logical. Optional thicker outline for UI icons. |
36: | Shading | Flat fill + 1–2 shade steps max (cel). Specular only on gold/gems/ice. No soft airbrush gradients on sprites. |
37: | Proportions | Haulers ~**48×48** gameplay frame (see inventory); slightly exaggerated heads; arms free to hold/throw. |
38: | Animation | Snappy 8–12 fps for run; hold-friendly idle; “compelled” states (Hurt/Stunned/Falling) override clearly. |
39: | Textures | Tileable blocks 32×32; seams intentional only for crumbling/receding feedback. |
40: | Anti-alias | Prefer **nearest-neighbor** friendly art (pixel-aligned). Soft AA allowed on UI panels/logo only. |
41: 
42: ### 3.2 Forbidden / avoid
43: 
44: - Photoreal materials, PBR, film grain
45: - Blood, gore, sexualized design
46: - Tiny unreadable jewelry as primary treasure silhouettes
47: - Pure black full-screen UI (use deep navy/charcoal with gold accents)
48: - Biome-tinted character body colors that break seat identity
49: 
50: ### 3.3 References (mood, not copy)
51: 
52: - Title: stick haulers + block letters (design §1.2 / §5.4 mockups)
53: - Controls diagram: NES pad clarity (§2.1)
54: - End: four colored vertical panels + treasure pile starburst (§1.5)
55: - High scores: portrait tiles + “New!” ribbon (§1.7)
56: - Parallax stack: Far / Near / Mid / Fore / Interface (§3.3)
57: 
58: ---
59: 
60: ## 4. Character identity
61: 
62: | Character | Primary hue | Secondary | Silhouette notes | Seat color token |
63: |---|---|---|---|---|
64: | **Gnome** | Amber / orange `#F0A040` | Brown hat/boots | Short, pointed hat, stocky | Orange panel |
65: | **Sprite** | Sky blue `#50A0E8` | White/silver wing accents | Slightly taller/lighter; optional wing nubs (still 2D side) | Blue panel |
66: | **Halfling** | Magenta / pink `#E070B0` | Warm tan skin | Rounder, curly hair cue | Pink panel |
67: | **Dwarf** | Crimson / red `#E05040` | Dark beard, metal buckle | Broadest torso, shortest legs | Red panel |
68: 
69: **Consistency rules**
70: 
71: 1. Same rig / frame grid / pivot for all four haulers (swap palette + costume parts).
72: 2. Carry stack mounts at a shared **carry anchor** above head; coin sacks do **not** raise stack height (design §2.2).
73: 3. Facing: art drawn facing right; flip for left.
74: 4. AI-controlled seats may show a small “AI” badge (optional P1) but body art is identical.
75: 
76: ---
77: 
78: ## 5. Palette system
79: 
80: ### 5.1 Global / UI
81: 
82: | Role | Hex (approx) | Use |
83: |---|---|---|
84: | Canvas letterbox | `#0B0B12` | Outside 960×540 |
85: | UI ink | `#1A1A22` | Text body |
86: | UI paper | `#F4EFE4` | Panels, instructions bg |
87: | Gold accent | `#E8C040` | Logo, unique rewards, +gp |
88: | Unique reward (Gold) | `#D4A017` | Share title panels |
89: | Common reward (White) | `#F5F5F5` | Share titles |
90: | Common penalty (Blue) | `#3A6BC4` | Share titles |
91: | Unique penalty (Red) | `#C03030` | Share titles |
92: | “New!” ribbon | `#FFE28A` | High score highlight |
93: | Safe highlight | `#40E0A0` | Ready, positive pulse |
94: | Danger | `#FF5040` | Spikes, gas warn (with shape) |
95: 
96: ### 5.2 Biome palettes
97: 
98: Each biome: **BG far**, **BG mid**, **block body**, **block edge**, **accent prop**, **hazard**.
99: 
100: | Biome | Far BG | Near/Mid mood | Blocks | Accent | Hazard |
101: |---|---|---|---|---|---|
102: | **Gold (Hoard)** | Deep vault purple `#2A1840` | Warm gold haze `#5A4020` | Aged stone + gold trim | Coin piles, candelabra | Low; sparkle only |
103: | **Outside** | Sky blue `#78B4E8` | Grass green `#4A9A40` | Dirt / stone path | Trees, clouds, fence | Pits (visual cliff) |
104: | **Dungeon** | Charcoal `#1E2430` | Cool grey stone | Brick grey `#6A6E78` | Torches, banners, grates | Spikes, iron gates |
105: | **Lava** | Ember black `#1A0A08` | Magma orange `#C04010` | Basalt / scorched brick | Lava glow, cracks | Lava pits, heat shimmer (VFX) |
106: | **Ice** | Pale cyan `#C8E8F8` | Frozen blue `#70B0D0` | Ice tile cyan/white | Icicles, frost | Slippery sheen on ice blocks |
107: | **Cavern** | Brown-black `#1C1410` | Earth brown `#6A4A30` | Rough rock | Stalactites, mushrooms | Rockfall shadows |
108: | **Mist** | Desat purple `#3A3050` | Fog lavender `#8A78A8` | Soft stone, vines | Wisps, hanging moss | Reduced contrast (keep colliders clear) |
109: 
110: **Rule:** Midground blocks must retain ≥ **4:1** contrast vs character primary hues for that biome’s typical BG.
111: 
112: ### 5.3 Treasure rarity readout
113: 
114: | Rarity | Visual cue |
115: |---|---|
116: | Common | Matte metals, small sparkle 0–1 |
117: | Rare | Stronger metal/gem cut, continuous soft glint |
118: | Unique | Distinct silhouette + gold outline pulse on idle |
119: | Set piece | Shared set badge color rim; complete-set VFX on end count |
120: | Chest | Closed box form; open reveals flash then swaps to treasure sprite |
121: 
122: ---
123: 
124: ## 6. Typography & logo
125: 
126: | Use | Recommendation | Notes |
127: |---|---|---|
128: | Logo wordmark “DUNGEON” | Bold display (e.g. **Marcellus SC** or similar SC) | Design §5.2 Megan list |
129: | Logo “HAUL” letters | Physical **block letters** carried on title (H/A/U/L props) | Matches mockup §1.2 |
130: | UI body | Clean pixel or rounded sans readable at 16–20 px | Prefer open counters |
131: | Numbers (+gp, %) | Tabular / monospaced digits | End count + high scores |
132: | Share titles | Same body, color-coded by panel type | No share **values** on titles (design) |
133: 
134: **Logo lockup:** “DUNGEON” above; four haulers with H-A-U-L blocks; tagline “Press Any Button” / online “Create or Join”.
135: 
136: ---
137: 
138: ## 7. Screen composition notes
139: 
140: | Screen | Camera | Visual priorities |
141: |---|---|---|
142: | **Title** | Fixed; scrolling far BG | Logo, walk-in haulers, idle sway, run-off on start |
143: | **Credits** | Fixed | Team cards / animated team graphic; TOJam 8 credit |
144: | **High Scores** | Fixed; list scrolls | Portrait tiles, GP, %, “New!” strip, last-run footer |
145: | **Lobby** *(online)* | Fixed | Room code, 4 seat slots, character claim portraits, ready |
146: | **Instructions** | **Fixed**, no zoom | Large control diagram; minimal ground; drop-in top-left |
147: | **Hoard / Level** | Multi-target follow | Parallax stack; carry stacks; traps readable |
148: | **Fork** | Fixed | Two biome-themed exits; path select + argue mash feedback |
149: | **End** | Cinematic pans | Exit order → treasure toss → share panels → rummage → take |
150: 
151: Safe margins: **16 px** from logical edges for critical UI; interface layer always on top.
152: 
153: ---
154: 
155: ## 8. Parallax stack (presentation contract)
156: 
157: Matches C-02 / design §3.3:
158: 
159: | Layer | Scroll vs mid | Content |
160: |---|---|---|
161: | Far (~50%) | 0.5× | Sky/cave mass, large silhouettes, tileable strip |
162: | Near (~100%) | 1.0× | Tall props filling height (columns, trees, ice pillars) |
163: | Mid | 1.0× | Blocks, traps, haulers, treasure, enemies |
164: | Fore (~125%) | 1.25× | Overhangs, vines, mist wisps in front of play |
165: | Interface | Screen-space | +gp floats, share panels, HUD, argue bubbles |
166: 
167: ---
168: 
169: ## 9. Animation principles
170: 
171: 1. **Involuntary overrides** (Hurt, Stunned, Falling) snap from any state (design §2.1).
172: 2. **One-shot actions** (Throw, Drop, Push/Trip, Jump) return to Idle/Run.
173: 3. **Weight feedback:** optional squash on land when heavy stack; no need unique art if VFX + anim speed suffice for MVP.
174: 4. **Spill:** treasure becomes free world sprites with bounce; hauler plays Hurt/Stunned + short pickup lockout (no special “naked” sprite required).
175: 5. **Argue (Fork):** hauler talk-bubble or arm-wave frames; at least 3 exclamation variants in audio—visual can reuse 2–3 mouth/pose frames.
176: 
177: ---
178: 
179: ## 10. Atlas & production constraints
180: 
181: | Constraint | Spec |
182: |---|---|
183: | Logical canvas | **960×540** |
184: | World block | **32×32** (architecture assumption) |
185: | Hauler frame | **48×48** preferred (fit in 2 blocks tall visually) |
186: | Treasure | **32×32** common; **32×40** tall uniques/sets OK |
187: | Trap tile | **32×32** base; multi-tile for golem/hand |
188: | Prefer atlas sizes | Power-of-two: 512, 1024, 2048 |
189: | Pipeline | Placeholder colored rects → swap-friendly **atlas keys** (C-02) |
190: | Naming | `cat_name_variant_frame` e.g. `char_gnome_run_02` |
191: 
192: Placeholder policy: solid color + letter label is shippable for engineering; **P0 art** replaces before playtest milestone “full loop readable”.
193: 
194: ---
195: 
196: ## 11. Consistency checklist (sign-off)
197: 
198: - [ ] Four haulers share frame grid, pivots, carry anchor
199: - [ ] Character hues match end panels, lobby seats, high-score portraits
200: - [ ] Spikes/gas/lightning never color-only (shape + motion)
201: - [ ] Coin sacks visually “soft” stack (no height add)
202: - [ ] Every biome has distinct far BG + 3 near props + block set
203: - [ ] UI share colors: gold / white / blue / red only for those roles
204: - [ ] All screens compose at 960×540 with 16 px safe margin
205: - [ ] No isometric or top-down tiles in production art
206:

208:

1: # Contract: Share Modifier & Treasure Rules (Pure API)
2: 
3: **Package:** `packages/rules` (planned)  
4: **Producers:** Rules Engine  
5: **Consumers:** Authoritative Simulation (end of run), unit tests, End Screen Director (display only)  
6: **Constraint:** **Pure functions** — no I/O, no engine, no network.
7: 
8: Canonical design: design doc §0.0, §2.2, §2.3 (and premise share list). Where premise and §2.3 tables differ slightly, **§2.3 tables win** unless noted.
9: 
10: ---
11: 
12: ## Public API surface
13: 
14: ```text
15: // --- Treasure valuation ---
16: getTreasureDef(defId: string): TreasureDef
17: rollTreasureDef(rng: Rng, table: "world" | "wooden_chest" | "silver_chest" | "gold_chest" | "magic_chest", ctx: RollContext): TreasureDef
18: computeInventoryValue(inventories: SeatInventory[], setCatalog?: SetDef[]): {
19:   totalGp: number
20:   perSeatGp: { seatId, gp }[]
21:   setCompletions: { setId: string, bonusGp: number, contributors: seatId[] }[]
22: }
23: // SeatInventory = { seatId, items: TreasureInstance[] }
24: // (Updated 2026-07-20 at implementation: instances carry no owner, so seat
25: // attribution must come from the caller; a flat TreasureInstance[] is still
26: // accepted and attributed to seat 0 for fixture convenience.)
27: 
28: // --- Weight / movement modifiers ---
29: computeEncumbrance(carryCount: number, carryWeight: number): {
30:   speedMultiplier: number
31:   jumpMultiplier: number
32:   // after first 3 treasures: cumulative decrease (exact curve parameterized)
33: }
34: 
35: // --- Stats aggregation helpers ---
36: // (optional) reduce event log → PlayerStats
37: 
38: // --- Share modifiers ---
39: evaluateModifiers(ctx: ScoreContext): PlayerModifierResult[]
40: 
41: computeTakes(totalTreasureGp: number, results: PlayerModifierResult[]): TakeBreakdown
42: 
43: // --- Catalog ---
44: listModifierDefs(): ShareModifierDef[]
45: rulesetVersion: string
46: ```
47: 
48: All functions must be **deterministic** given the same inputs + RNG stream.
49: 
50: ---
51: 
52: ## Core types
53: 
54: ```text
55: ScoreContext {
56:   seats: {
57:     seatId: number
58:     character: CharacterId
59:     human: bool
60:     stats: PlayerStats
61:     finalInventory: TreasureInstance[]
62:     hoardExitInventoryCount: number
63:   }[]
64:   levelsCompleted: number
65:   // precomputed relatives:
66:   ranking: {
67:     mostTreasureValue: seatId[]
68:     mostTrapsHit: seatId[]
69:     mostHitsDealt: seatId[]
70:     mostHitsTaken: seatId[]
71:     mostTreasureLost: seatId[]
72:     mostAirTime: seatId[]
73:     leastAirTime: seatId[]
74:     alwaysFirstExit: seatId[]   // Leader of the Pack candidates
75:     alwaysLastExit: seatId[]
76:   }
77: }
78: 
79: PlayerStats {
80:   // see ARCHITECTURE.md §8 — full counter set
81: }
82: 
83: PlayerModifierResult {
84:   seatId: number
85:   modifiers: AppliedModifier[]
86:   rawShares: number
87:   shares: number              // max(1, rawShares) per seat after all deltas
88: }
89: 
90: AppliedModifier {
91:   id: string
92:   title: string
93:   kind: "reward" | "penalty"
94:   uniqueness: "unique" | "common"
95:   deltaShares: number
96: }
97: 
98: TakeBreakdown {
99:   totalTreasureGp: number
100:   totalShares: number
101:   players: {
102:     seatId: number
103:     shares: number
104:     sharePercent: number      // shares/totalShares * 100
105:     takeGp: number            // floor or round policy — document: **floor to int GP**, remainder to highest share seat
106:   }[]
107: }
108: ```
109: 
110: ### Payout formula
111: 
112: ```text
113: take_i = TotalTreasureGp * (shares_i / sum(shares))
114: shares_i = max(1, sum(deltaShares_i))
115: ```
116: 
117: **Min 1 share** always, even if penalties would reduce below 1.
118: 
119: ---
120: 
121: ## Modifier catalog (implement & test)
122: 
123: ### Rewards (design §2.3)
124: 
125: | ID | Title | Δ | Condition |
126: |---|---|---|---|
127: | leader_pack | Leader of the Pack | +10 | Always first to exit each level |
128: | breadwinner | Breadwinner | +5 | Most treasure value recovered |
129: | airhead | Airhead | +3 | Most airtime |
130: | landshark | Landshark | +3 | Least airtime |
131: | jammy | Jammy | +1 | Brought Goat on a Pole |
132: | haul | Haul | +1 / item | Each treasure recovered |
133: | collector | Collector | +1 / set piece | Each set piece in a completed set |

145: | ID | Title | Δ | Condition |

162:

173: 
174: Show share percentages in order **3rd, 2nd, 4th, 1st** place (by take or share rank — **assume by final takeGp**).
175:

🕹️ 1. NES Control Layout

Dungeon Haul uses a clean, responsive NES-style control scheme designed for maximum clarity during high-speed slapstick moments:

NES GAMEPAD MAPPING
DPAD / WASD

Run Left / Right
Duck / Pick Up Loot

BUTTON A / SPACE

Jump / Rise
Hover (Sprite)

BUTTON B / K

Shoulder Push / Trip
Drop / Throw Stack

DOWN + B

Fast Drop Treasure
Clear Top Stack Item

🔄 2. The Gameplay Loop

  1. Lobby & Seat Claim: Four haulers enter a private room code. Claim your class (Gnome, Sprite, Halfling, Dwarf) and toggle ready.
  2. Level 0 Treasure Hoard: The run begins in a treasure-packed vault room! Grab as many burlap sacks, crowns, and chests as you can carry.
  3. Fork Voting Chamber: At the end of each level, vote on the next biome path (e.g. Lava vs. Ice). Button-mash to argue your choice and sway the group!
  4. Dungeon Escape: Navigate dangerous biomes, hit switches, dodge spike traps, and trip opponents to steal their top stack items.
  5. End Payout & Share Titles: Upon escaping, arcane Share Modifiers are evaluated. Earn titles, calculate final GP shares, and top the high-score leaderboard!

⚖️ 3. Encumbrance & Carry Stack

Haulers carry treasures in a vertical stack above their head.

  4. Dungeon Escape: Navigate dangerous biomes, hit switches, dodge spike traps, and trip opponents to steal their top stack items.
  5. End Payout & Share Titles: Upon escaping, arcane Share Modifiers are evaluated on the server. Earn titles, calculate final GP shares, and top the high-score leaderboard!

⚖️ 4. Encumbrance & Carry Stack

Haulers carry treasures in a vertical stack above their head.

  • First 3 treasures can be carried with zero movement penalty.
  • Additional items beyond 3 cause a cumulative decrease in run speed and jump height.
  • Greed Overwhelming occurs if speed drops to zero — making you an easy target for shoulder pushes!
  • If injured or stunned, your carry stack spills Sonic-style across the room!

🧮 5. Share Formula & Payout

Your final Gold Piece (GP) take is determined by the server payout formula:

Player Take = Total Dungeon GP × ( Player Shares / Sum of All Shares )

* Note: Every hauler receives a guaranteed minimum of 1 share, even if penalties would otherwise reduce their total below zero!
